evals.query: Search the internet for the top 10 news stories from today.
evals.expected_output: A digest titled 'Top 10 News — Global — <today's date>' with 10 numbered entries, each with a bold headline, a 1–2 sentence neutral summary, and a source line with outlet, HH:MM time with timezone and a [link], ending with a one-line 'Sources & method' note.
expected_behavior: Runs `date` first to establish today's date and timezone and tells the user the date and scope (Global) before searching
Runs 4–6 web searches combining the date and scope, including wire services or major outlets
Verifies publish times and drops any story that cannot be dated
Runs scripts/validate_digest.py and only presents the digest after it reports ok: true
Output follows templates/digest.md: title, numbered entries with bold headlines, source lines with '· [link](...)', and a 'Sources & method' line
No more than 2 items come from the same outlet and no duplicate events or URLs appear
Every URL comes from a search result or fetched page; no invented facts or times

evals.expected_output: A digest titled 'Top 10 News — Japan — <today's date>' focused on stories about or directly affecting Japan, using Japan-specific query recipes and outlets such as NHK World, Kyodo, Japan Times or Nikkei Asia, with times shown in the user's timezone.
expected_behavior: Treats 'Japan' from $ARGUMENTS as the scope and states it before searching
Uses the country query recipes from reference/ranking-criteria.md (e.g. NHK World, Kyodo, Japan Times, Nikkei Asia, Reuters Japan)
Keeps only stories about Japan or directly affecting it, excluding generic global stories that merely mention it
Passes --tz-offset from the `date +%z` output and renders with --scope "Japan"
Developing or unconfirmed stories carry a label and appear as '[Developing]' or '[Unconfirmed]' in the headline
Validator returns ok: true before the digest is presented

evals.query: What's the biggest tech news today? Give me a top 10 briefing.
evals.expected_output: A topic-scoped digest (e.g. 'Top 10 News — Tech — <date>') of today's tech stories drawn from tier-1/tier-2 and specialist outlets, respecting the 3-per-sub-topic and 2-per-outlet caps; if fewer than 10 verifiable stories exist, the title uses the real count and a shortfall line explains the list was not padded.
expected_behavior: Interprets the plain-language request as a tech topic scope
Searches sub-topics (AI, security, regulation, chips, devices, platforms) and specialist outlets such as The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica or Reuters technology
Applies the sub-topic cap (at most 3 per sub-topic) and outlet cap (at most 2 per outlet)
Merges duplicate coverage of the same event and cites the most authoritative source, preferring original wire copy over republishers
If fewer than 10 stories can be verified, uses --expect N, titles the digest 'Top N News', includes the shortfall line and does not pad
Summaries are neutral, at most 60 words and drawn only from article or snippet text

evals.query: Give me today's top headlines for the UK. Some results I found were live blogs updated today about stories from last week.
evals.expected_output: A UK-scoped digest where live blogs are included only if they report a new development today (described in the summary, possibly labelled 'updated'), stale stories are replaced, and the validator's stale/duplicate errors are resolved before presenting.
expected_behavior: Includes live blogs only when there is a new development today and describes that development
Uses the 'updated' label for items whose main development is an update to an older story
Replaces any item the validator flags as stale, undated or duplicate with the next-best verified candidate and re-runs validation
Cites original wire services (e.g. PA Media, Reuters) rather than republishers of syndicated copy
Presents the digest with date, scope 'UK' and a one-line sources & method note
